threads.body: [General] The PR description promises a maximum-idle-connections metric, but this creates only the maximum-total-connections measurement; the test also explicitly asserts that `db.client.connection.idle.max` / `db.client.connections.idle.max` is absent. Emit `metrics.maxIdleConnections()` (using the Redisson pool limit if that is the maximum idle capacity) and cover it in the test, or remove maximum idle connections from the advertised behavior if Redisson cannot provide that value.

This puts the resolved IP into `pool.name`, while the 2.3-3.17 module in #19152 builds the same name from `address.getHostString()`. So the same Redis endpoint gets a different pool name depending on which Redisson version you're on. `getHostString()` is also what the existing Redisson span instrumentation (`RedissonDbAttributesGetter`) already uses for `server.address`, so matching it keeps the two consistent. And it costs nothing — `getHostString()` is the accessor that deliberately avoids reverse DNS.

```suggestion
    String host = address.getHostString();
```

(the `InetAddress` import becomes unused)

[Testing] Parameterize so the pending-request count can be asserted as non-zero.

```suggestion
  private static void assertPendingRequests(
      String regularPool, long regularPending, String subscriptionPool, long subscriptionPending) {
    testing.waitAndAssertMetrics(
        INSTRUMENTATION_NAME,
        emitStableDatabaseSemconv()
            ? "db.client.connection.pending_requests"
            : "db.client.connections.pending_requests",
        metrics ->
            metrics.anySatisfy(
                metric ->
                    assertThat(metric)
                        .hasUnit(emitStableDatabaseSemconv() ? "{request}" : "{requests}")
                        .hasDescription(
                            emitStableDatabaseSemconv()
                                ? "The number of current pending requests for an open connection."
                                : "The number of pending requests for an open connection, cumulative for the entire pool.")
                        .hasLongSumSatisfying(
                            sum ->
                                sum.isNotMonotonic()
                                    .hasPointsSatisfying(
                                        point ->
                                            point
                                                .hasValue(regularPending)
                                                .hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
                                                    equalTo(stringKey(poolNameKey()), regularPool)),
                                        point ->
                                            point
                                                .hasValue(subscriptionPending)
                                                .hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
                                                    equalTo(
                                                        stringKey(poolNameKey()),
                                                        subscriptionPool))))));
```

`nodeType` shouldn't be part of the pool name. It's a role, not an identity: the address already identifies the node, so the prefix buys no uniqueness. `MasterSlaveEntry.setupMasterEntry` creates the master entry and then also calls `addSlave(client.getAddr(), ..., NodeType.MASTER, ...)`, so there are already two entries at the same address both named `master-*`.

What it does add is instability. On failover `slaveBalancer.changeType(...)` flips a live entry between MASTER and SLAVE without replacing its `RedisClient`, and the name captured here in the constructor never catches up, so a pool keeps reporting under a role it no longer has.

Dropping it leaves `<host>:<port>` plus the regular/subscription split, which lines up with the approach `JdbcConnectionPoolNameUtil` settled on in #19371: derive from the address, no role or sequence discriminator, and let pools to the same server aggregate.

The other two Redisson modules use `display_name: Redisson`, and `docs/contributing/documenting-instrumentation.md` describes display name as what collapses related modules into one entry. This PR also keeps Redisson as a single row in supported-libraries.md, so a separate display name here splits it back out.

```suggestion
display_name: Redisson
```
